# Siana — Architecture, city by city

> Siana is an editorial atlas of architecture: a curated guide to significant buildings around the world, mapped city by city, paired with Practice — essays, field notes, and practical guides for architects.

Siana documents notable architecture across global cities and writes about it with an editorial eye. The site is organized into three areas: **Cities** (city guides with an interactive map of pinned buildings), **Projects** (individual buildings with architect, year and context), and **Practice** (essays, criticism, profiles, interviews, field notes, and practical guides for architecture, engineering and construction practices).

- Website: https://sianaarchitecture.com
- Language: English
- Focus: architecture, cities, urbanism, design history, the built environment
- Cities covered: Barcelona, Chicago, Copenhagen, Lisbon, Mexico City, Porto

## Cities
- [Barcelona](https://sianaarchitecture.com/cities/barcelona): Architecture guide to Barcelona, Spain — Modernisme, mosaics, and the unfinished cathedral of a dream.
- [Chicago](https://sianaarchitecture.com/cities/chicago): Architecture guide to Chicago, United States — The birthplace of the skyscraper.
- [Copenhagen](https://sianaarchitecture.com/cities/copenhagen): Architecture guide to Copenhagen, Denmark — Quiet Nordic rigor by the water.
- [Lisbon](https://sianaarchitecture.com/cities/lisbon): Architecture guide to Lisbon, Portugal — Azulejo light spilling across seven hills.
- [Mexico City](https://sianaarchitecture.com/cities/mexico-city): Architecture guide to Mexico City, Mexico — Barragán's color and the weight of volcanic stone.
- [Porto](https://sianaarchitecture.com/cities/porto): Architecture guide to Porto, Portugal — Granite, fog, and the precision of Siza.

## Practice
- [The Drawing That Thinks Back](https://sianaarchitecture.com/practice/the-drawing-that-thinks-back): Architecture + AI — Generative tools promise infinite variation. What they ask in return is a new kind of authorship.
- [On the Patience of Stone](https://sianaarchitecture.com/practice/on-the-patience-of-stone): Essay — Why the slowest buildings often outlast the fashions that surround them.
- [The Museum That Forgot Its Street](https://sianaarchitecture.com/practice/the-museum-that-forgot-its-street): Criticism — A new cultural landmark dazzles from the water and turns its back on the city behind it.
- [Lina Bo Bardi, In Her Own Light](https://sianaarchitecture.com/practice/lina-bo-bardi-in-her-own-light): Profile — The architect who treated concrete as an invitation rather than a barrier.
- [A Conversation With the Last Brickmaker](https://sianaarchitecture.com/practice/a-conversation-with-the-last-brickmaker): Interview — Forty years at the kiln, and a quiet argument for materials that age in public.
- [Lisbon, From the Tile Up](https://sianaarchitecture.com/practice/lisbon-from-the-tile-up): City guide — A walking route through azulejo facades, hillside miradouros and the quiet genius of the pombaline grid.
- [The Slow Return of the Courtyard](https://sianaarchitecture.com/practice/the-slow-return-of-the-courtyard): Reportage — Across three continents, architects are rediscovering the oldest trick for cooling a city block.

## Projects
- [8 House](https://sianaarchitecture.com/projects/8-house): BIG, 2010 — Copenhagen.
- [Altos de Lima](https://sianaarchitecture.com/projects/altos-de-lima): Javier F — Barcelona.
- [Casa Batlló](https://sianaarchitecture.com/projects/casa-batllo): Antoni Gaudí, 1906 — Barcelona.
- [Casa da Música](https://sianaarchitecture.com/projects/casa-da-musica): OMA / Rem Koolhaas, 2005 — Porto.
- [Casa Luis Barragán](https://sianaarchitecture.com/projects/casa-luis-barragan): Luis Barragán, 1948 — Mexico City.
- [Champalimaud Centre](https://sianaarchitecture.com/projects/champalimaud-centre): Charles Correa, 2010 — Lisbon.
- [MAAT](https://sianaarchitecture.com/projects/maat-lisbon): Amanda Levete (AL_A), 2016 — Lisbon.
- [Mercat de Santa Caterina](https://sianaarchitecture.com/projects/mercat-santa-caterina): EMBT, 2005 — Barcelona.
- [Museo Soumaya](https://sianaarchitecture.com/projects/museo-soumaya): FR-EE / Fernando Romero, 2011 — Mexico City.
- [Robie House](https://sianaarchitecture.com/projects/robie-house): Frank Lloyd Wright, 1910 — Chicago.
- [Royal Danish Opera](https://sianaarchitecture.com/projects/royal-danish-opera): Henning Larsen, 2005 — Copenhagen.
- [Sagrada Família](https://sianaarchitecture.com/projects/sagrada-familia): Antoni Gaudí, 1882 — Barcelona.
- [Serralves Museum](https://sianaarchitecture.com/projects/serralves-museum): Álvaro Siza, 1999 — Porto.
- [Willis Tower](https://sianaarchitecture.com/projects/willis-tower): SOM / Fazlur Rahman Khan, 1973 — Chicago.

## Main sections
- [Atlas](https://sianaarchitecture.com/atlas): Interactive map — explore every project by city, architect, style and year.
- [Cities index](https://sianaarchitecture.com/cities): Browse all cities in the atlas.
- [Practice](https://sianaarchitecture.com/practice): Essays, field notes, and practical guides for architecture, engineering and construction practices.
- [About](https://sianaarchitecture.com/about): What Siana is and why it exists.
